title: Diamond and Suslin trees: prediction and construction
summary: Diamond implies CH and anticipates maximal antichains in a recursive construction of a Suslin tree.
abstract: Diamond is a prediction principle at the first uncountable ordinal: one sequence guesses each subset correctly on initial segments whose endpoints meet every closed unbounded set. Assuming this principle, the real line has the smallest possible uncountable size, as asserted by the continuum hypothesis. The same predictions also yield a Suslin tree: a tree reaching the first uncountable height in which every chain of comparable nodes and every antichain of mutually incomparable nodes is countable. Thus diamond controls both the size of the real line and the existence of an uncountable tree with no uncountable chain or antichain.
